risks.description: Macroeconomic volatility and subnational fiscal distress caused by oil price collapses may constrain state-level implementation capacity and domestic public funding.
risks.mitigation: Provide 100 percent IDA credit financing for total project costs without requiring mandatory counterpart cash contributions from participating state governments.
risks.evidence: The collapse of oil prices and the liquidity crunch revived tensions between federal government and subnational governments regarding burden of the adjustment

risks.description: Militancy and security instability in regions such as the Niger Delta and North East could disrupt field supervision, infrastructure works, and agricultural supply chains.
risks.mitigation: Adopt flexible state/cluster resource allocation, conduct local security assessments, and rely on community-level engagement for project implementation.
risks.evidence: sharp drop in oil production levels due to militant activities in the Niger Delta region.

risks.description: Delays in executing and securing legal opinions for Subsidiary Agreements between the Federal Government and participating states may delay project effectiveness and disbursements.
risks.mitigation: Enforce disbursement conditions requiring authorized subsidiary agreements and satisfactory legal opinions prior to releasing funds to any participating state.
risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made under Categories (1), (2), and (3)... unless the Association has received an opinion

risks.description: Financial management weaknesses regarding unretired travel advances and inadequate documentation in PFMUs and FPFMD could cause ineligible expenditures and audit qualifications.
risks.mitigation: Implement an enhanced accountability framework in the Financial Procedures Manual, including risk-based internal audits and strict advance acquittal enforcement.
risks.evidence: The key issues noted within the PFMUs and FPFMD are unretired advances and inadequate documentation of the eligible expenditures incurred.

risks.description: Weak procurement capacity in state coordination offices and required executive approval thresholds at state levels could cause procurement delays and slippages.
risks.mitigation: Competitively recruit qualified procurement specialists, hire a technical procurement consultant to support state offices, and utilize standardized national bidding documents.
risks.evidence: The procurement capacity is still considered low and most of the states do not have procurement tools in place.

risks.description: Agricultural intensification and increased usage of agro-chemicals (pesticides, synthetic fertilizers) could lead to soil contamination, surface water pollution, and health hazards.
risks.mitigation: Implement an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) and ESMF screening procedures to promote climate-smart agriculture and safe pesticide handling.
risks.evidence: agricultural intensification involving the use of inputs, could potentially have adverse impact on soil, water and vegetation covers.

risks.description: Civil works for processing infrastructure, aggregation centers, and access roads may lead to land acquisition, physical displacement, or restricted access to common resources.
risks.mitigation: Apply the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) to screen sub-project sites and prepare Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) providing fair compensation before works begin.
risks.evidence: infrastructure investments could result in involuntary re-settlement and land requisition.

risks.description: Installation of utility connections, transmission lines, or gas pipelines for processing clusters could encroach upon sensitive natural habitats such as wetlands and marshes.
risks.mitigation: Enforce OP/BP 4.04 Natural Habitats screening protocols within the ESMF to ensure sub-project infrastructure avoids sensitive ecological zones.
risks.evidence: extension of electricity transmission lines and installation of gas pipelines might pass through important natural habitats such as swamps and marshes.

risks.description: Financial and economic viability is highly sensitive to drops in commodity market prices, where a 20 percent reduction in benefit values causes negative NPVs.
risks.mitigation: Develop structured business alliances with off-takers, support commodity aggregation centers, and invest in primary processing to stabilize producer prices and prevent post-harvest losses.
risks.evidence: if benefits were reduced by 20 percent for all the crops, the net present values will turn negative

risks.description: Gender gaps in access to land, agricultural inputs, credit, and extension services could prevent female farmers and entrepreneurs from benefiting from project investments.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Women and Youth Empowerment sub-component with dedicated grant funding, business development services, mentorship, and gender-tracked M&E indicators.
risks.evidence: women in Nigeria, compared with men, have relatively limited access to productive agricultural land, inputs and services.

risks.description: Delays in competitively recruiting and deploying new APPEALS implementation staff from existing CADP structures could slow initial implementation momentum.
risks.mitigation: Retain existing CADP operational staff using government funding during an 18-month transitional period while competitive recruitment is conducted.
risks.evidence: During the first 18-month period of project implementation, it is expected that selection and replacement of CADP staff will be completed

risks.description: Multi-tiered institutional arrangements across federal and state bodies (NSC, NCO, SSC, STC, SCO, PFMU) risk operational misalignment and bureaucratic bottlenecks.
risks.mitigation: Define clear roles and responsibilities in the Project Implementation Manual, schedule structured quarterly STC and annual SSC meetings, and establish regular progress reporting.
risks.evidence: Project implementation will involve both the federal and state governments. The project will be executed jointly by the NCO at the federal level and SCOs

risks.description: Prevalence of adulterated or substandard agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, chemicals) in local markets could severely undermine productivity gains.
risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to FMARD and national regulatory agencies to strengthen quality assurance, seed certification, and agro-dealer accreditation.
risks.evidence: capacity strengthening on quality control of agro-inputs such as seeds, fertilizer and agro-chemicals to address issues of adulteration

risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder communication or unaddressed community grievances regarding sub-project selection and benefit distribution could result in local conflict or dissatisfaction.
risks.mitigation: Establish a comprehensive Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), implement a strategic communication and outreach campaign, and monitor citizen engagement metrics.
risks.evidence: Percentage of grievances registered, related to delivery of project benefits that are actually addressed
